note:
The household of Edmund Pratt, lace manufacturer, at **4 Pelham Terrace** on the 1891 return - the house now numbered **35 Newcastle Drive** (#225), named **Pelham House** and built about 1860. Transcribed from the census image by Claude at A. Hagues's request; the readings are mine and the doubtful ones are flagged below. 35 Newcastle Drive held only 1921, so 1891 is free, and none of the seven was in the record.

**The placement is by the conversion rule**, not by a source naming this house: Newcastle Drive was formerly Pelham Terrace, and 39 minus the Pelham Terrace number gives the Newcastle Drive number, fixed by two confirmed pairs - 12 to 27 (Glendower, the Fosters) and 24 to 15. 39 - 4 = 35. Two things support it beyond the arithmetic: 35 is the one house on this stretch that carries a name, Pelham House, which is what one would expect of the first substantial villa on a street called Pelham Terrace; and a lace manufacturer with a wife, three grown daughters and two servants fits a house of that size. It is still a conversion rather than a direct identification, so if the rule is ever disproved this household moves with a single reassign. See [[newcastle-drive-pelham-terrace-numbers]].

**Readings to check:** the housemaid's surname, which I read as Summ and which is probably incomplete; her age, read as 18; and Sarah Ann Franklin's birthplace, read as Raceby in Lincolnshire, which may be Ranceby or Rauceby. Ages are as the enumerator wrote them, so a birth year worked back from one may be a year out either way.
source: 1891 census, 4 Pelham Terrace (now 35 Newcastle Drive, Pelham House), read from the census image supplied by A. Hagues.
